body:
This looks dangerous to me. You are re-ordering the existing SpecularMode enums (so that e.g. someone who set it to DISABLED will suddenly have TOON Specular after updating their engine version).

Also, is there a reason why Multiscatter is not the default? I am aware that it only really makes a difference for metallic materials, but I would argue that it should still be enabled per default. I doubt most users know the difference between Multiscatter/Schlick GGX and when to enable which and it's not like it is an expensive difference instruction wise.

(Hell, is there even a reason to keep Schlick GGX? Wouldn't it make more sense to just replace it entirely on forward+ while falling back to it on the mobile renderer?)

I am not certain how much sense it makes to print this warning. It is a well known fact that the compat renderer is not designed for the utmost visual quality, so imo it should just silently fall back to Schlick. There is no reason to warn the user about something they can't change.

As above, I am fairly certain this will break compat. And again, I would just merge Schlick and Multiscatter into a single option (which is renamed to "GGX") that behaves differently depending on the renderer in use.
Once more, this warning won't really help the user. There is nothing they can do about it.

vec2 dfg = prefiltered_dfg(roughness, cNdotV).xy;

I do think it should be disabled when reading the DFG LUT for multiscattering, as it could also impact performance.

I implemented it this way because I noticed a warning is triggered for each feature that doesn't work on Mobile and Compatibility. Even if we decide to keep multiscattering as default, this warning would still be relevant since multiscattering won't work on Mobile and Compatibility due to the lack of a DFG LUT - which I'm in favor of not adding.

I implemented it this way because Blender and O3DE allow switching between single scattering and multiscattering, since multiscattering only affects rough metallic materials. However, I'm not opposed to keeping SchlickGGX as is and only applying multiscattering in Forward+ - but we'll need to warn users about this one way or another.

body:
I am sorry, I don't quite understand your comment.

Let me try to rephrase how I envision this all working out: The `SpecularMode::SPECULAR_SCHLICK_GGX` enum is renamed to `SpecularMode::SPECULAR_GGX` and behaves differently depending on the current platform:

1. On Forward+ it always uses the DFG LUT and multiscattering.
2. On mobile/compat it does **not** use the DFG LUT or multiscattering and instead uses the approximation from unreal we have right now.

This way no new enum needs to be added, projects using forward+ are automatically upgraded and there is no performance loss on mobile/compat.
It should be added at the end to not break compatibility

One of the main problems with adding this as an optional drop down is discoverability. I am not sure how many people even know what the difference between single scattering and multi scattering is, and forcing people to manually update every single material in their project to enable it is just bad UX.

Also, what happens when people want to ship their game on both Desktop (with forward+) and old android devices (using compat)? Ideally, the process of supporting both rendering backend should be as seamless as possible, so unifying the setting (and calling it `SPECULAR_GGX`) makes the most sense to me.

I honestly don't really see the point in supporting single scattering in forward+. Our goal with Forward+ is to build a general purpose, high quality and fairly accurate renderer, and that means including multiscattering.

If people don't want to use it in their game for stylistic reasons, they can use a shader template with SchlickGGX instead.
If you want different targets you just use export specific options, you just add a dedicated option setting for each, that's normal to pick

The thing is that Schlick_GGX is outdated and should be deprecated. The only reason why it still in Godot is that A) nobody had bothered to make a PR yet and B) the approximation is needed due to performance constraints on mobile devices.

As far as I can remember last week's rendering meeting, we were all in agreement that once we have multiscattering it should just replace Schlick on desktop.

body: I wouldn't touch the specular enum at all. But other than that I agree. We can use the DFG LUT and the multiscatter approximation on Forward+, but keep the old approximation for Mobile and Compatibility. There is no need to expose a setting

To ensure consistent behavior between renders, I had to apply the BRDF in the same way it is applied in the approximation, and the reason it is inverted is because a modified DFG is being used, as indicated by Google Filament.
`A += (1.0f - Fc) * G_Vis;` -> `A += Fc * G_Vis;`
`B += Fc * G_Vis;` -> `B += G_Vis;`

This is how Google Filament applies the BRDF:
https://google.github.io/filament/Filament.html#listing_multiscatteriblevaluation https://github.com/google/filament/blob/main/shaders/src/surface_light_indirect.fs#L136-L146.

If you notice, what they do is quite strange because they don't take f90 into account, only f0, resulting in the following:
![Screenshot1](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/fc2803c6-8820-44bb-ba8b-61e15084e013)
![Screenshot2](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0f428dbb-4e63-4aa8-9a5b-5f43d89a1a8d)

There’s also a version where they multiply it by pixel.specular, but I don’t quite understand how this works, since even if it’s just the raw specular parameter, the results still end up wrong.

body:
Something like this:

`[b]Note:[/b] Mobile and Compatibility don't perform multiscattering for performance reasons. Instead, they perform single scattering, which means rough metallic surfaces may look slightly darker than intended.`

Also, I would merge the first warning with the above note (as it's essentially a continuation of that note).

In short, these should be the two remaining notes:

```
[b]Note:[/b] Forward+ uses multiple specular lobes (multiscattering) for more accurate reflections, at a slight performance cost. The impact of multiscattering is most noticeable on rough metallic surfaces. For smooth surfaces and non-metal surfaces, the impact likely won't be noticed.
[b]Note:[/b] Mobile and Compatibility don't perform multiscattering for performance reasons. Instead, they perform single scattering, which means rough metallic surfaces may look slightly darker than intended.
```

PS: `won’t` uses a smart quote in your PR, please replace it with an ASCII quote too (`won't`).

```suggestion
		float f90 = clamp(50.0 * f0.g, metallic, 1.0);
```

This needs to use metallic as the bottom of the range to match the behaviour before. See for the full context for why we differ from filament https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/69522
Thanks for pointing out that detail to me. We have to be very careful with the calculations that Google Filament proposes.
